questions.title: Settling-bead viscosity and independent density
questions.stem:
A model laboratory dataset is used to investigate a viscous liquid. A solid calibration body of known volume $4.00\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^3}$ has balance readings $0.03120\,\mathrm{kg}$ in air and $0.02640\,\mathrm{kg}$ when fully immersed. Ignore air buoyancy. Use $g=9.81\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Spherical steel beads of density $\rho_s=7800\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ settle through the same liquid. The plotted terminal speeds have uncertainty $\pm0.5\,\mathrm{mm\,s^{-1}}$; radius-squared uncertainties are negligible. After assessing the graph, use the reported gradient $s=(12.0\pm0.4)\,(\mathrm{mm\,s^{-1}})/\mathrm{mm^2}$ for subsequent calculations. The independent density measurement gives $\rho_l=(1200\pm75)\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

For terminal Stokes motion, $v_t=2g(\rho_s-\rho_l)r^2/(9\eta)$. Treat $g$ and $\rho_s$ as exact. A second test examines the validity of the Stokes model using the supplied diagnostic $\mathrm{Re}=2\rho_lrv_t/\eta$; the model is more reliable when $\mathrm{Re}\ll1$.

steps.text: The lost apparent mass is $0.00480\,\mathrm{kg}$ and buoyancy gives $(m_{air}-m_{immersed})g=\rho_lVg$.
The plotted error bars are consistent with a straight line through the origin; this supports the proportional model over this measured range, without proving it universally.
$\eta=2g(\rho_s-\rho_l)/(9s)=1.199\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}$.
$\Delta\eta/\eta=75/(7800-1200)+0.4/12.0=0.044697$. The numerator is a density difference, so use its absolute uncertainty before dividing.
$\eta=(1.20\pm0.05)\,\mathrm{Pa\,s}$; an appropriately rounded equivalent such as $1.199\pm0.054$ is accepted.
The largest bead has $r=\sqrt{3.24}\,\mathrm{mm}=1.8\,\mathrm{mm}$ and $v_t=0.0388\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, giving $\mathrm{Re}=0.140$.
This is below one but not arbitrarily small; smaller beads reduce $r$ and $v_t$, lowering Re and improving the creeping-flow approximation.

Low Re alone does not prove terminal motion. Check that equal later time intervals give equal displacements, or that a late displacement-time trace has constant gradient; otherwise the force balance used for $v_t$ is invalid.

questions.stem:
A model vacuum-chamber investigation tests radiative power from a coated tile. Its area is known and its emissivity is assumed temperature-independent. Chamber walls stay at $T_0=300\,\mathrm K$. The measured net outward radiative power per area is $J=\varepsilon\sigma(T^4-T_0^4)$, where $\sigma=5.67\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,K^{-4}}$. Conduction through supports is negligible.

| $T/\mathrm K$ | 600 | 700 | 800 | 900 | 1000 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $J/(\mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}})$ | 5.50 | 10.5 | 18.2 | 29.4 | 45.0 |

Each measured $J$ has uncertainty $\pm0.50\,\mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$. The graph uses $X=(T^4-T_0^4)/(10^{11}\,\mathrm{K^4})$. A fit through the origin gives gradient $(4.54\pm0.08)\,\mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$ per unit $X$. Treat temperature uncertainties as negligible in parts(a)–(c).
